titulo: AI Bots Drive Majority of Pro-Bolsonaro Tweets, Study Finds
resumo: A study by UFRJ and FespSP found that AI-driven bots and automated accounts were responsible for 55% of 1.2 million pro-Bolsonaro tweets using #BolsonaroDay. The coordinated bot activity manipulated political discourse on Twitter, raising concerns about AI's role in influencing public opinion and undermining democratic processes.

titulo: Trump Campaign Uses AI-Generated Audio to Falsely Attribute 'Hoax' Comment to Biden
resumo: The Trump campaign released a manipulated audio clip, likely created with AI tools, falsely making it appear Joe Biden called the coronavirus a "hoax." This synthetic media was used to retaliate against similar accusations and highlights the use of AI in spreading political misinformation, risking public harm and undermining democratic discourse.

titulo: AI Moderation Shortfalls During Lockdown Linked to Rise in Online Child Abuse
resumo: During the COVID-19 lockdown, social networks like Facebook and Twitter increased reliance on AI for content moderation due to reduced human oversight. titulo: Pandemic-Era AI Surveillance Raises Global Privacy Concerns
resumo: Governments worldwide have deployed AI-enabled smartphone geolocation and contact tracing to contain COVID-19, prompting human rights groups to warn of potential privacy violations and threats to civil liberties. titulo: Massive Sale of Masked Face Photos for AI Training Sparks Privacy Fears in China
resumo: Vast numbers of masked face photos, sourced from social media, workplace check-ins, and public surveillance, are being illegally collected and sold online in China for AI facial recognition training. resumo: TuSimple and ZF have partnered to co-develop and commercialize AI-driven autonomous truck technologies, including sensors and control systems, for global markets. titulo: Exaggerated Claims of AI Outperforming Doctors in Medical Imaging Raise Safety Concerns
resumo: Multiple studies claiming AI matches or surpasses doctors in interpreting medical images are of poor quality and often exaggerated, according to researchers. resumo: During the Covid-19 pandemic, governments worldwide deployed AI-enabled facial recognition and smartphone tracking systems to monitor and enforce quarantine measures. resumo: Hong Kong research teams and startups deployed AI-based fever detection and contact tracing systems at border checkpoints and public venues to identify and isolate potential COVID-19 cases. titulo: Stanford Study Finds Racial Bias in Major Voice Recognition AI Systems
resumo: A Stanford University study found that voice recognition AI systems from Apple, Google, Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft have significant racial bias, with much higher error rates for African American users compared to white users. This bias leads to discriminatory outcomes and unequal access to technology.

titulo: Facial Recognition AI in Moscow Courts Leads to Detention of Supporters at Hearings
resumo: Moscow courts covertly deployed facial recognition AI, resulting in the detention of six individuals who attended hearings to support defendants in protest-related cases. The system identified people wanted by police, raising concerns about privacy and human rights violations due to AI-driven surveillance in judicial settings.

resumo: Russian traffic authorities are testing AI-powered cameras using neural networks to detect drivers using mobile phones while driving. resumo: Chinese researchers developed an AI system to analyze Covid-19 patient data and predict survival rates, directly influencing doctors' decisions on treatment prioritization. titulo: Smart Speakers' AI Raise Privacy Concerns for Remote Workers
resumo: Law firm Mishcon de Reya and others warned employees to mute or turn off AI-powered smart speakers like Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant while working from home, after incidents of these devices unintentionally recording confidential conversations, raising concerns about privacy breaches and unauthorized data collection by AI systems.

titulo: Polish Government Deploys AI App for Quarantine Enforcement
resumo: The Polish government launched the 'Kwarantanna domowa' app, which uses facial recognition and geolocation AI to monitor individuals under quarantine. Users must send periodic selfies to confirm their location. While intended for public health, the system raises concerns about privacy and potential misuse, though no harm has been reported yet.

titulo: Volvo Recalls Over 700,000 Vehicles Due to AI-Driven Emergency Braking System Malfunction
resumo: Volvo recalled over 700,000 vehicles globally from model years 2019-2020 after discovering a software defect in the AI-powered automatic emergency braking system, which may fail to detect obstacles or pedestrians, increasing crash risk. No injuries have been reported, and a software update is being provided to fix the issue.

titulo: AI-Powered Surveillance in East Asia Raises Privacy and Human Rights Concerns During COVID-19 Response
resumo: China, Taiwan, and South Korea used AI-driven facial recognition, big data analytics, and mobile tracking to identify and control COVID-19 cases, achieving significant virus suppression. titulo: Tesla Autopilot Design Flaws and Regulatory Gaps Blamed in Fatal 2019 Crash
resumo: A fatal 2019 crash in Florida involving a Tesla on Autopilot was attributed to the AI system's design flaws, which allowed driver inattention and activation in inappropriate conditions. resumo: Spanish police deployed AI-enabled drones in Madrid to monitor public spaces and instruct citizens to stay home during the COVID-19 lockdown. resumo: AI-generated deepfakes have been used in phishing scams and financial fraud, causing real harm to individuals and businesses.
